# Critical Issues Checklist: Backend Security & Judge Correctness

**Purpose**: Validate that the backend's requirements cover the critical security, trust-boundary, and judge-correctness issues identified in the code audit — before any implementation work begins.
**Created**: 2026-08-02
**Feature**: No spec.md exists for the backend; requirements below are derived from the full backend audit (security & integrity + judge correctness findings). This checklist tests whether each critical requirement is documented, clear, consistent, and measurable.

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Security & Trust Boundaries

- [ ] CHK001 Is a requirement documented that match judging MUST evaluate submissions against server-side expected outputs (retrieved from the stored problem) rather than any client-supplied expected values? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for authenticating socket connections (e.g., JWT handshake) before any user-identifying event (`online`, matchmaking, submission) is accepted? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 Is a requirement specified that the submitting socket must be verified as one of the match's players before its submission is processed or affects match state? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Is a secrets-management requirement defined stating that JWT, refresh-token, internal-secret, and database credentials must never be committed to version control, including a rotation policy? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for every user-facing response specifying which fields must be excluded (e.g., password hashes) so no sensitive data is serialized? [Completeness]
- [ ] CHK006 Is an authorization requirement specified for rating/stat update endpoints, defining ownership checks (actor id must equal target id) and roles, separate from mere token validity? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK007 Is an access-control requirement defined for match-history queries, restricting users to their own records? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK008 Are requirements defined classifying every endpoint as public, authenticated, or internal, and is that classification consistent with the middleware applied to each route? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK009 Are rate-limiting requirements specified for authentication endpoints (login/register) with quantified thresholds and lockout behavior? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK010 Is a threat model documented for the judge pipeline covering untrusted code execution and client-supplied payloads, with requirements traced to it? [Traceability]

## Judge Correctness (Code Execution)

- [ ] CHK011 Is a requirement defined that every supported language's full judge path (compile/run, normalize, compare, pass/fail determination) is part of the acceptance contract and must behave identically across languages? [Completeness]
- [ ] CHK012 Are output-normalization requirements (case, whitespace, float precision, boolean aliases) defined and stated to apply consistently to ALL supported languages, with no implicit per-language exceptions? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK013 Are resource-limit requirements (memory, CPU, wall-clock time, output size, network access) specified per language with concrete values rather than a single shared default? [Clarity]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the pass/fail determination requirement specified unambiguously for each judge type (float, boolean, string, ignore_case), including comparison semantics? [Clarity]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for per-language build steps (e.g., C++ compilation) with budgets distinct from execution budgets, so compilation resource use is explicit? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 Are sandboxing requirements specified for code execution (non-root user, network isolation on all flows, capability drops, process limits, stdout caps)? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK017 Is a requirement defined that judge pipeline failures must surface explicitly rather than being converted into a pass or fail verdict? [Exception Flow]

## Match Integrity & Lifecycle

- [ ] CHK018 Is a requirement defined that a match is finalized exactly once (winner determination, Elo update, persistence) even under concurrent submissions from both players? [Gap, Scenario Coverage]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for match termination when the timer expires, including winner determination and Elo/persistence handling? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK020 Is a requirement defined for matchmaking queue cleanup on disconnect (removal from queue, prevention of stale-socket matches)? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK021 Is a requirement specified that players are verified as connected before a match is created? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for match-room lifecycle in memory, including expiry, cleanup, and a single source of truth for room state? [Completeness]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements specified for validating matchmaking input (rating bounds, user identity), including defined rating-range limits aligned with queue capacity? [Edge Case Coverage]
- [ ] CHK024 Are recovery requirements defined when Elo finalization or persistence fails (retry/rollback semantics, user-visible outcome, residual state)? [Recovery]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements specified that all client-supplied inputs are validated to prevent process-level failures (no uncaught-exception crash paths)? [Completeness]
- [ ] CHK026 Are performance requirements defined for matchmaking operations with bounds independent of queue size? [Clarity]
- [ ] CHK027 Are memory-management requirements defined for all unbounded in-memory stores (rooms, matchmaking nodes, pending connections), including eviction and cleanup policies? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK028 Are availability requirements specified for the server under malicious load (unauthenticated execution, room creation), with quantified limits per endpoint? [Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK029 Is a scaling assumption documented for socket/matchmaking state (single instance vs. multi-instance with shared state), and is the chosen model consistent across all stateful components? [Assumption]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality & Traceability

- [ ] CHK030 Does every requirement above have measurable acceptance criteria (quantified thresholds, exact verdict semantics, defined exclusion lists)? [Acceptance Criteria]
- [ ] CHK031 Is a requirement-ID scheme established for the security, judge, and match-integrity requirement sets to enable traceability? [Traceability]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the recovery and exception scenarios (judge failure, DB failure, disconnect mid-match, concurrent submission) explicitly listed in the requirements as in-scope, not implicitly handled? [Coverage]

## Notes

- Check items off as completed: `[x]`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
